I'm in a polyamorous relationship with two guys (also male here), and I can tell you first-hand that it's not as hard as it may seem. The most important thing about finding a poly relationship is the same as with most other relationships. Remember this. Shell Silverstein was an awesome guy.

You don't have to know exactly what you're looking for in a poly relationship. If you want to have a very strong hand in where your life goes and how things unfold, then you may want to take the 'alpha' route and be in charge of selecting both your partners. You may find a couple whose goals are very compatible with yours, and joining the relationship can be incredibly rewarding, because there's this already-existing dynamic you can get wrapped up in and become a new and fun part of.

It's alright not to completely understand what you're trying to make, and to expect your partner(s) to be supportive of you figuring that out, even if that ultimately means you decide not to stay with them. Being in a poly relationship isn't any harder than being in a normal one; you're just exchanging one set of problems for another.

But because I was open about what I was looking for, there are some people I never would have thought (and they themselves never would have thought) would be ok with this, and yet, here we happily are several years on.

And it wasn't on the first try, either, we didn't get it right for awhile. I've lost a partner or two, and even both at the same time once, which was pretty hard. But getting it right is incredibly rewarding and we're very happy.

You're not a freak, you're not weird, and you don't have to 'settle' for people willing to be in a poly situation for you. Just get out there, be who you are, and the right people will take notice.
